The modeling of EM behavior of VLSI systems is becoming increasingly important as clock frequencies increase and signal rise times decrease.
The higher spectral content of signals and more complicated structures increase the complexity of EM models required.
MOR techniques can simplify the analysis of EM models by reducing the number of degrees of freedom.
Parabolic DEs or diffusion problems are well-suited for MOR techniques.
Hyperbolic problems are challenging for MOR techniques due to the large number of relevant eigenvalues.
The number of eigenvalues can easily exceed 10^3 for high-performance EM problems.
The first test problem involves coupled lossless transmission lines with a 9-conductor problem.
The second test problem is a 2D printed circuit board problem with a ferrite core.
The ferrite core represents a decoupling element that reduces noise transferred to the isolated quiet part of the plane.
The ultimate goal of the paper is to develop reliable MOR techniques for EM problems that can efficiently solve large-scale problems.
The special IEEE Transactions issue on MOR techniques represents the state-of-the-art on MOR techniques.
The challenge of recovering all the resonances from data is a very challenging problem.
The paper presents two test problems to compare the different MOR approaches.
The first test problem involves a 9-conductor transmission line problem with a 5cm and 15cm length.
The second test problem involves a 2D printed circuit board problem with a ferrite core and a regular array of decoupling capacitors.
The paper highlights the challenges and opportunities in applying MOR techniques to EM problems.
